indication: Indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma (follicular lymphoma, marginal zone lymphoma)
investor_note: This Phase 1/2 trial aims to establish the RP2D and early efficacy signal for EO2463, a novel cancer vaccine, as monotherapy and in combination with lenalidomide and/or rituximab in indolent NHL — a proof-of-concept read that could validate the microbiome-mimicry vaccine platform. Key caveats are the non-randomized design, long timeline to primary completion (2029), and the early-phase nature of the study, meaning any efficacy data will be hypothesis-generating rather than registrational.

indication: Advanced or metastatic NSCLC (non-squamous and squamous), 1L
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 study evaluates rulonilimab (F520), a PD-1 inhibitor, combined with standard chemotherapy backbones in first-line advanced/metastatic NSCLC across two histology cohorts; a compelling ORR would support advancement to a randomized registrational trial. Key caveats are the single-arm, open-label design with no comparator arm, making it hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing on its own.

indication: Nab-paclitaxel-induced peripheral neuropathy in breast cancer
investor_note: This randomized trial tests whether hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) can meaningfully reduce chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) symptoms and improve quality of life in breast cancer patients treated with nab-paclitaxel, using the patient-reported EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 as the primary endpoint. A positive result would validate HBOT as a supportive-care intervention in CIPN, though the academic sponsorship, non-commercial device modality, and PRO-based primary endpoint limit direct investable catalysts for industry.

indication: HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, ≥3L
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 evaluates utidelone (an epothilone analog) plus bevacizumab (anti-VEGF) in heavily pre-treated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with PFS as the key efficacy signal to watch. The absence of a comparator arm and single-arm design limit interpretability; results would be hypothesis-generating rather than registrational without a follow-on randomized study.

indication: Untreated metastatic (stage IV) nasopharyngeal carcinoma, 1L
investor_note: This completed single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated the anti-EGFR antibody nimotuzumab added to cisplatin/5-FU chemotherapy in first-line metastatic NPC, with ORR and PFS as co-primary endpoints — results would be hypothesis-generating for the combination but cannot establish causality without a comparator arm. The small enrollment (n=39), lack of randomization, and academic sponsorship mean any signal requires validation in a controlled, adequately powered study before commercial relevance can be assessed.

indication: Solid tumors with soft tissue metastases
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored trial tests whether adding autologous myeloid dendritic cells (myDC) to intratumoral ipilimumab + AS01B adjuvant plus systemic nivolumab improves safety and efficacy over the checkpoint/adjuvant combo alone in solid tumors — a proof-of-concept for DC-based intratumoral immunotherapy. With only 18 estimated patients across 2 arms and a mixed safety/feasibility/efficacy primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating signal study with no near-term registrational implications.

indication: Recurrent or metastatic breast cancer
investor_note: This dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD and safety profile of bortezomib (a proteasome inhibitor) combined with cisplatin in recurrent/metastatic breast cancer, with preliminary efficacy as a secondary signal. With only 20 estimated patients across 6 arms and a purely safety-focused primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating, early-stage academic study — not a registrational catalyst.

indication: Malignant peritoneal mesothelioma, 1L
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether adding PIPAC (pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy with cisplatin + doxorubicin) to standard systemic cisplatin/pemetrexed improves OS in first-line malignant peritoneal mesothelioma — a rare, high-unmet-need indication. The trial is currently suspended and is academically sponsored, limiting near-term commercial catalyst value; any OS signal would be hypothesis-generating rather than registrational.

indication: Hematologic malignancies (ALL, AML, MDS, CML, NHL, others) undergoing allogeneic HCT
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether high-dose pre-conditioning vitamin A and D3 supplementation reduces the cumulative incidence of gastrointestinal acute GVHD following allogeneic HCT — a clinically meaningful and commercially underexplored complication. The academic sponsorship and non-proprietary intervention limit direct commercial upside, but a positive result could validate a low-cost supportive-care strategy and inform adjunctive protocols for sponsors developing GVHD therapeutics.

indication: Relapsed/refractory AML or ALL, 2L+
investor_note: This completed investigator-sponsored Phase 2 trial assessed the response rate of high-dose cytarabine plus clofarabine in a heavily pretreated, poor-prognosis AML/ALL population; a meaningful ORR would support the combination as a salvage bridge-to-transplant regimen. Single-arm design with only 39 patients limits generalizability, and the trial is already completed — value lies in historical efficacy/safety data rather than a prospective catalyst.

indication: Advanced solid tumors (malignant neoplasms), all-comers
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation trial sought to establish the MTD/MAD of ombrabulin (a vascular-disrupting agent) combined with bevacizumab (an anti-VEGF antibody) in unselected solid tumor patients; the key output is a tolerable RP2D for the combination, not efficacy. With only 39 patients enrolled in a single-arm, non-randomized design, results are hypothesis-generating at best and would require a larger randomized study to establish clinical benefit.

indication: Advanced/metastatic solid tumors (broad, unselected)
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation/expansion study establishes the safety profile, MTD, and recommended Phase 2 dose of DB-1305/BNT325 (a novel ADC, also tested in combination with pembrolizumab and BNT327) across a broad solid tumor population; the key catalyst is early tolerability data and any preliminary efficacy signal that could guide indication selection. With 30 arms and an estimated 1,123 patients, the trial is ambitious in scope but remains primarily a safety/dose-finding exercise with a long readout horizon through H2 2027.

indication: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC)
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated BKM120 (buparlisib), an oral pan-PI3K inhibitor, in TNBC — a setting with few targeted options — using clinical benefit rate as the primary endpoint. The absence of a comparator arm and use of a surrogate efficacy endpoint limit the strength of any positive signal for registration purposes.

indication: Basal cell carcinoma (post-surgical reconstruction)
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored Phase 2 trial evaluates a tissue-engineered autologous skin substitute (PHITAH/PHIT) versus standard skin autograft for wound reconstruction following basal cell carcinoma surgery, with co-primary safety and efficacy endpoints. With only 21 estimated enrollees and academic sponsorship, results will be hypothesis-generating for the bioengineered skin field rather than registrational, and the primary completion date of January 2024 suggests data may already be available or imminent.

indication: Stage IV metastatic or locally recurrent NSCLC, post-immunotherapy progression
investor_note: This withdrawn trial (zero patients enrolled) aimed to test whether a single 10 Gy fraction of radiotherapy to one progressing lesion is non-inferior to multi-fraction schedules in re-inducing systemic immune response in stage IV NSCLC patients who progressed on immunotherapy. As the trial was withdrawn before enrollment, there is no investable catalyst — any future re-activation would require a new registration and protocol review.

indication: Adenocarcinoma of the esophagus or esophagogastric junction, palliative (non-curative intent)
investor_note: This single-arm academic trial tests whether palliative short-course hypofractionated radiotherapy (5×4 Gy) followed by oxaliplatin/fluorouracil chemotherapy meaningfully relieves dysphagia in inoperable esophageal/GEJ adenocarcinoma patients. With only 29 patients, no comparator arm, and a symptom-based primary endpoint, results are hypothesis-generating only and carry no direct registrational or commercial catalyst value.

indication: Relapsed/refractory hematologic malignancies (CLL, MCL, DLBCL, FL, MZL, and others), previously treated
investor_note: This completed first-in-human dose-escalation study established the MTD and recommended dosing regimen for zilovertamab vedotin (a ROR1-targeting ADC) across a broad range of B-cell and T-cell hematologic malignancies. The key investor catalyst was safety/tolerability de-risking and identification of the RP2D to support subsequent registrational-intent studies; efficacy signals in specific subtypes (e.g., MCL, DLBCL) would be hypothesis-generating only at this stage.

indication: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia / lymphoblastic lymphoma
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored, single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluates DA-EPOCH (with TKI augmentation via dasatinib/imatinib) in ALL/lymphoblastic lymphoma, using morphological CR and MRD clearance as co-primary endpoints — both surrogates for long-term benefit. The trial is now completed; results would be hypothesis-generating for a TKI-augmented chemotherapy regimen but carry limited commercial weight given the academic, non-randomized design.

indication: Resectable locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, neoadjuvant
investor_note: This single-arm academic study evaluates the neoadjuvant triplet of camrelizumab (PD-1 inhibitor), chemotherapy, and apatinib (VEGFR TKI) ahead of surgery in resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, with pCR as the key signal-finding endpoint. A meaningful pCR rate would be hypothesis-generating for a randomized trial, but the small, non-randomized design and surrogate endpoint limit direct commercial or regulatory conclusions.

indication: High-risk prostate cancer (extraprostatic disease detection)
investor_note: This trial was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient (actual enrollment = 0), meaning no data on the diagnostic performance (sensitivity/specificity) of the [89Zr]Df-IAB2M PET/CT imaging agent in high-risk prostate cancer will be generated from this study. The withdrawn status is the dominant investor signal — the program's viability and any future catalyst depend entirely on whether ImaginAb relaunches the study under a revised protocol.

indication: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC), neoadjuvant setting
investor_note: This small investigator-sponsored study tests whether 12 weeks of neoadjuvant sonidegib (Hedgehog pathway inhibitor) can downsize BCC tumors sufficiently to reduce surgical morbidity or enable topical-only follow-up, assessed by optical coherence tomography — a non-standard imaging endpoint. With only 16 patients enrolled across 3 non-randomized arms, results are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no direct registrational value for sonidegib's label.

indication: Hematologic malignancies undergoing non-myeloablative allogeneic stem cell transplantation (GVHD prophylaxis)
investor_note: This completed academic Phase 2 trial assessed whether a triple immunosuppressive regimen (sirolimus + tacrolimus + methotrexate) could reduce GVHD incidence and severity following non-myeloablative allogeneic transplant in hematologic malignancies. With no comparator arm and a non-randomized design, findings are hypothesis-generating only and would require a randomized trial to establish superiority over standard two-drug prophylaxis.

indication: HER2-negative early breast cancer, neoadjuvant
investor_note: This randomized, double-blind Phase 2 trial evaluated whether adding lapatinib (TKI) to letrozole (aromatase inhibitor) improves clinical objective response in HER2-negative early breast cancer in the neoadjuvant setting — a hypothesis-testing study for a combination that has since lost commercial relevance given lapatinib's declining use. The trial is completed and the primary endpoint (cOR) is a surrogate; no OS data are generated, limiting regulatory and commercial impact.

indication: HPV16+ advanced/recurrent non-resectable cervical cancer, 2L+
investor_note: This Phase 2a single-arm study tests whether combining VB10.16 (a therapeutic cancer vaccine targeting HPV16) with atezolizumab (PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor) can generate meaningful responses in a biomarker-selected, treatment-refractory cervical cancer population — a positive ORR would support advancement to a randomized trial. Key caveats are the single-arm design with no comparator, making it difficult to attribute benefit to the vaccine component over atezolizumab alone, and the surrogate ORR endpoint in a small, niche population.

indication: Advanced/metastatic breast cancer (HR+/HER2-, TNBC) and metastatic colorectal cancer
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation/expansion study establishes the safety, MTD, and preliminary anti-tumor activity (ORR in Part 2) of Pfizer's novel oral agent PF-08032562 as monotherapy and in combination with standard-of-care regimens across breast and colorectal cancer subtypes. The primary catalyst is identification of a recommended Phase 2 dose and early efficacy signals in the expansion cohorts; the multi-arm, non-randomized design and long ~4-year timeline mean meaningful data are unlikely before late decade.

indication: MAGE-A3+ non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC)
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored Phase 1 study evaluates whether intravesical BCG schedules can potentiate systemic and local immune responses to a MAGE-A3 cancer vaccine (ASCI) in NMIBC patients, with safety/tolerability as the primary endpoint. With only 23 patients, no randomization, and a completed status, this is a purely exploratory immunology signal-finding study — any commercial relevance hinges on whether the immunogenicity data support further development of the MAGE-A3 ASCI platform.

indication: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
investor_note: This registrational Phase 3 trial pits SYS6002 (a CSPC Megalith ADC) head-to-head against investigator's choice chemotherapy in advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma, with OS as the gold-standard primary endpoint — a positive result would support a label in this indication. Key caveats are the pre-ethics-approval status (recruitment not yet started), the long ~3-year timeline to primary readout, and limited public data on SYS6002's earlier-phase efficacy profile.

indication: Breast cancer risk reduction in radiation-induced cancer survivors
investor_note: This randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2b trial tests whether low-dose tamoxifen citrate reduces mammographic breast density — a surrogate for breast cancer risk — in survivors of radiation-induced cancer. The primary readout is a surrogate imaging endpoint (mammographic density), not a clinical cancer incidence outcome, limiting direct regulatory translation without a larger confirmatory trial.

indication: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), 2L+
investor_note: This trial, combining the dendritic cell vaccine DCVAC/PCa with oncolytic virus ONCOS-102 in heavily pre-treated mCRPC, was terminated after enrolling only 5 patients — rendering any efficacy or safety conclusions unreliable. The termination and minimal accrual represent a significant setback for this combination immunotherapy program, and investors should treat this asset as substantially de-risked downward until SOTIO provides a clear rationale and path forward.

indication: HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether prophylactic loperamide and cetirizine can meaningfully reduce the incidence of grade ≥2 diarrhea and rash — the two most common dose-limiting toxicities of capivasertib — in HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer patients on capivasertib plus fulvestrant. A positive result would support a tolerability-improvement strategy that could broaden real-world uptake of capivasertib (AstraZeneca/Sanofi's CAPItello-291-approved regimen), but this trial does not address efficacy and carries no direct approval pathway of its own.

indication: Advanced adenocarcinoma of the prostate
investor_note: This completed pilot study enrolled only 3 patients to assess the safety of UbiVac's DRibble vaccine (with cyclophosphamide, HPV vaccine, and imiquimod as adjuncts) in advanced prostate cancer — the catalyst is purely safety signal generation, not efficacy. With an actual enrollment of 3, results are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no statistical weight for informing a larger program without further study.

indication: Breast cancer with comorbid major depressive episode
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial aimed to compare antidepressant efficacy of citalopram vs. psychotherapy in breast cancer patients with major depression, using BDI score change as the primary endpoint — a non-standard oncology outcome with limited commercial relevance. The trial was terminated with only 40 actual enrollees and a primary completion date matching the start date, indicating it generated no meaningful efficacy data and carries no near-term catalyst value.

indication: Advanced non-hematologic malignancies (pancreatic, head & neck, prostate neoplasms)
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation trial evaluated the safety, PK, and pharmacodynamic activity of PF-00562271, a FAK/PYK2 inhibitor, across multiple solid tumor types using FDG-PET metabolic response as a bioactivity readout. As a completed early-phase study, its investor relevance lies primarily in the DLT/MTD profile and any PET-based signal that could justify further development of FAK inhibition in these indications.

indication: Small cell lung cancer (extensive and limited stage)
investor_note: This SWOG-led registrational trial tests whether MRI surveillance alone is non-inferior to prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) plus MRI in SCLC, with OS as the gold-standard endpoint — a result favoring MRI-only could shift standard of care away from routine PCI. The open-label design is the primary methodological caveat, though blinding is impractical in a radiation vs. no-radiation comparison.

indication: Intermediate-risk squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN), adjuvant
investor_note: This single-arm academic study tests whether durvalumab (PD-L1 inhibitor) combined with adjuvant radiotherapy can improve 3-year DFS while reducing toxicity versus the cisplatin-RT standard in intermediate-risk SCCHN — a hypothesis-generating signal, not a registrational dataset. With only 18 patients actually enrolled and no comparator arm, any efficacy signal would require validation in a larger randomized trial before it could support a label or partnership thesis.

indication: Recurrent Ewing's family of tumors or desmoplastic small round-cell tumor
investor_note: This completed single-arm Phase 2 trial assessed imatinib mesylate's ability to generate objective responses (per RECIST) in heavily pretreated Ewing's sarcoma family tumors and DSRCT — rare, high-unmet-need sarcomas with limited salvage options. Results are historical; the key caveat is the small, non-randomized design in a heterogeneous rare-tumor population, limiting generalizability without a comparator arm.

indication: Multiple brain metastases from solid tumors
investor_note: This proof-of-concept study evaluated tumor-vasculature-targeting radioimmunotherapy (131I-L19SIP) combined with whole-brain radiation in a small, non-randomized cohort of brain metastasis patients, with primary endpoints of tumor uptake and safety rather than survival or response. The trial is completed and serves as a signal-generating step only — the small single-arm design and surrogate/safety endpoints preclude any registrational conclusions without a controlled efficacy study.

indication: Relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation study of ADCLEC.syn1 CAR T cells aims to establish MTD/safety in a high-unmet-need R/R AML population where CAR T remains largely unproven; the key catalyst is tolerability data and any early efficacy signal at the RP2D-defining dose. With only 40 patients, a single arm, and a 4-year timeline, this is a pure safety/signal-finding study — not registrational evidence.

indication: Colorectal cancer, chemoprevention (newly diagnosed, pre-surgical)
investor_note: This mechanistic Phase 2 trial compares three aspirin dosing regimens in 60 newly diagnosed CRC patients to identify the optimal dose and COX acetylation biomarker signature for chemoprevention — the key catalyst is pharmacodynamic evidence linking a specific dose to maximal COX-1/COX-2 acetylation in tumor tissue. Results are hypothesis-generating for dose selection in future registrational chemoprevention trials, not themselves practice-changing; the surrogate biomarker primary endpoint and small academic design limit direct commercial read-through.

indication: Recurrent/advanced ovarian cancer (Stage III-IV), neoadjuvant setting
investor_note: This terminated academic Phase 1/2 trial was evaluating locoregional cisplatin combined with a chemokine modulatory regimen and autologous dendritic cell vaccines in advanced ovarian cancer, with immunologic response (CD8+ TILs) and safety as co-primary endpoints. Termination materially undermines any investment thesis — no efficacy or safety conclusions can be drawn from this record.

indication: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma (primary tumor <5 cm), 1L palliative
investor_note: This trial evaluates palliative radiofrequency ablation of the primary tumor prior to systemic therapy (interferon-alpha or sunitinib) in metastatic RCC, with PFS as the key signal; a positive result would support cytoreductive ablation as a morbidity-reducing bridge to systemic treatment. Non-randomized design across three arms and academic sponsorship limit generalizability — findings are hypothesis-generating rather than practice-defining.

indication: Relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation trial establishes the MTD and safety profile of oral KPT-9274 — a dual PAK4/NAMPT inhibitor — in a heavily pretreated R/R AML population; the key catalyst is whether a tolerable RP2D emerges to support a subsequent efficacy study. With only 16 patients enrolled across 6 arms, this is strictly a safety/dose-finding signal — no efficacy conclusions can be drawn.

indication: Recurrent ovarian cancer
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation trial established the RP2D of NUC-1031 (a ProTide gemcitabine analogue) combined with carboplatin in recurrent ovarian cancer, providing the safety foundation for any subsequent Phase 2 development. With only 25 patients in a single-arm, non-randomized design, the trial is purely a safety/dose-finding milestone — efficacy signals are exploratory and not registrational.

indication: Multiple myeloma, incomplete response to chemo pre-autologous stem cell transplant
investor_note: This single-arm pilot tested CD20-targeted radioimmunotherapy (Zevalin/ibritumomab tiuxetan) added to myeloablative chemo and autologous SCT in myeloma patients with residual disease, but the trial was terminated with only 8 patients enrolled — severely limiting any efficacy or safety conclusions. The terminated status and minimal accrual render this a non-actionable catalyst; no meaningful signal can be drawn from the dataset.

indication: Relapsed/refractory aggressive B-cell and T-cell lymphomas
investor_note: This trial was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient (actual enrollment = 0), meaning no safety, tolerability, or RP2D data were generated for the PLK1 inhibitor (volasertib) plus HDAC inhibitor (belinostat) combination. The withdrawal eliminates any near-term catalyst value; investors should monitor whether the sponsor or another group relaunches the combination in a revised protocol.

indication: Newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML), 1L
investor_note: This pilot trial evaluated the cardiac safety profile (LVEF reduction via MRI) and feasibility of standard 7+3 induction chemotherapy (cytarabine + daunorubicin) in newly diagnosed AML patients, with the trial now completed. As an academic-sponsored, single-arm safety/feasibility study with 40 patients, findings are hypothesis-generating around cardiotoxicity monitoring rather than efficacy-defining, limiting direct commercial catalyst value.

indication: PD-L1+, EGFR-mutated TKI-resistant advanced NSCLC
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored single-arm study tests whether the IO (pembrolizumab) + TKI (lenvatinib) combination can overcome TKI resistance in a dual biomarker-selected NSCLC population; a meaningful PFS signal would be hypothesis-generating for a randomized follow-on. With only 35 estimated patients, no comparator arm, and a surrogate PFS endpoint, results are signal-finding only and carry significant interpretation risk.

indication: Psoriasis, adalimumab monotherapy suboptimal responders
investor_note: This real-world, single-arm study assessed whether adding methotrexate to adalimumab rescues suboptimal responders in psoriasis, with both investigator- and patient-assessed response at Week 16 as co-primary endpoints. The very small actual enrollment (n=46), non-randomized open-label design, and surrogate response endpoints limit any registrational or label-expansion utility — findings are hypothesis-generating at best.

indication: Advanced sarcoma (multiple subtypes), relapsed/refractory
investor_note: This 7-cohort, non-randomized Phase 2 basket trial tests pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) plus metronomic cyclophosphamide — with or without G100 — across advanced sarcoma subtypes, using 6-month ORR and non-progression rate as co-primary endpoints. The key watch is whether any specific sarcoma subtype shows a durable response signal that could justify a registrational follow-on, though the non-randomized design and heterogeneous population limit direct causal attribution.

indication: Hepatic impairment (mild/moderate) — PK characterization in non-oncology population
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 PK study characterizes how hepatic impairment affects steady-state exposure to JNJ-38518168 (a Janssen small molecule), informing dose-adjustment guidance and label language rather than demonstrating efficacy. As a purely pharmacokinetic/regulatory support study with 28 subjects and no efficacy endpoint, it carries no direct catalyst value beyond enabling broader patient dosing in future trials.

indication: Adult brain metastases (poor prognosis)
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 non-inferiority trial tests whether a single-fraction 8 Gy regimen matches 20 Gy/5 fractions in overall survival for poor-prognosis brain metastasis patients — a result that would support a faster, simpler standard of care. The academic sponsorship and Phase 2 design limit direct commercial impact, but findings could influence practice and inform future registrational studies for radiotherapy device/service providers.

indication: Stage IIIa primary hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombosis
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluates whether intra-arterial H101 (oncolytic adenovirus) added to TACE improves disease control rate in a high-unmet-need HCC subpopulation with portal vein tumor thrombosis — a positive DCR signal would support further randomized development of oncolytic virus + locoregional therapy combinations. Key caveats are the very small estimated enrollment (38 patients), absence of a comparator arm, and use of DCR (a surrogate) as the primary endpoint, limiting the strength of any efficacy conclusions.

indication: Multiple myeloma / cutaneous lymphoma (hematopoietic stem cell mobilization)
investor_note: This first-in-combination Phase 1 trial evaluates the safety of ATRA + G-CSF as a novel HSPC mobilization strategy in patients with myeloma or cutaneous lymphoma who face high mobilization failure rates with current approaches. With only 6 patients enrolled and toxicity as the sole primary endpoint, this is a pure safety signal-generating study with no efficacy readout and minimal near-term commercial catalyst.

indication: High-risk MDS or AML
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored Phase 2 evaluated the proteasome inhibitor bortezomib combined with the HDAC inhibitor vorinostat in high-risk MDS/AML, with clinical response rate as the key endpoint. The trial was terminated early with only 16 patients enrolled — a significant red flag that substantially limits any efficacy conclusions and signals likely futility or safety concerns.

indication: Advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma, 1L
investor_note: This pilot trial evaluates the safety and feasibility of NovoCure's TTFields device (NovoTTF-100L, 150 kHz) layered onto standard gemcitabine or gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy in front-line pancreatic cancer — the key catalyst is whether device compliance and tolerability support advancement to a randomized efficacy study. With only 40 patients, no randomization, and safety/feasibility as co-primary endpoints, this is strictly a signal-generating and de-risking step, not a registrational dataset.

indication: Breast cancer with bone-dominant metastases, post-endocrine therapy
investor_note: This small single-arm study evaluated whether up to four doses of Radium-223 (Xofigo) produce clinically meaningful changes in bone turnover markers (uNTX, ALP) in endocrine-refractory breast cancer with bone-dominant disease — a surrogate signal-finding exercise, not an efficacy readout. With only 23 patients and no comparator, results are hypothesis-generating at best and cannot support a registration or label claim on their own.

indication: Neuroendocrine carcinoma
investor_note: This completed academic study evaluated whether 68Ga-DOTATATE PET imaging — a somatostatin receptor-targeted diagnostic — changes clinical management decisions versus conventional imaging in neuroendocrine carcinoma patients. The primary endpoint (rate of care-plan change) is a clinical utility measure rather than a survival or response endpoint, making this a diagnostic/theranostic platform validation rather than a traditional therapeutic efficacy trial.

indication: Advanced or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma, 1L (age ≥65)
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial (GERICO) tests whether oral cyclophosphamide can match or outperform standard doxorubicin on PFS in elderly STS patients, with a key secondary focus on tolerability and quality of life — a positive result could redefine first-line chemotherapy practice in this underserved age group. PFS as the primary endpoint (not OS) and the academic/cooperative group sponsorship limit near-term commercial catalyst value, but a win would carry meaningful label-shaping implications for the elderly STS population.

indication: FLT3-mutated AML (newly diagnosed, relapsed/refractory) or high-risk MDS
investor_note: This Phase 1/2 investigator-sponsored trial aims to establish the MTD/RP2D and then assess overall response rate for the oral hypomethylating agent ASTX727 combined with venetoclax and the FLT3 inhibitor gilteritinib in a biomarker-selected AML/MDS population. A strong ORR signal in the Phase 2 portion — particularly in the relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutated cohort — would be hypothesis-generating for a registrational combination strategy, but the single-arm, small-enrollment, academic design limits direct commercial read-through.

indication: HER2+ metastatic or locally advanced unresectable breast cancer
investor_note: This completed academic Phase 1 study characterized platelet function and thrombokinetic changes associated with trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) in HER2+ advanced breast cancer — a mechanistic safety investigation rather than an efficacy or registrational trial. With only 13 patients enrolled and a focus on a known ADC-class toxicity (thrombocytopenia), findings are hypothesis-generating for managing T-DM1's hematologic side effects, not a commercial catalyst.

indication: Hematological cancers (leukemia, MDS, MDS/MPN), allogeneic SCT setting
investor_note: This completed academic Phase 2 trial evaluated a busulfan/fludarabine/ATG conditioning regimen prior to allogeneic bone marrow transplant, with treatment-related mortality and engraftment as co-primary endpoints — procedural benchmarks rather than efficacy signals. As a single-arm, investigator-sponsored study at a single Korean center, findings are hypothesis-generating for conditioning regimen optimization but carry no direct registrational or near-term commercial catalyst value.

indication: Advanced metastatic pancreatic cancer, 1L
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial tests QL1706 (a dual PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) combined with lenvatinib (TKI) and gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy as first-line therapy in advanced pancreatic cancer, with mPFS as the key catalyst readout. The absence of a comparator arm and the use of PFS rather than OS limit the registrational weight of any positive signal, making this primarily hypothesis-generating for the IO+TKI+chemo triplet strategy in a notoriously difficult-to-treat tumor type.

indication: Relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation study evaluated the safety and MTD of imetelstat (GRN163L), a telomerase inhibitor, in heavily pre-treated myeloma patients — the catalyst was establishing a tolerable dose and early signals of activity, not efficacy. With only 20 patients enrolled and a DLT/MTD primary endpoint, this is a foundational safety study only; any efficacy signal would be purely exploratory.

indication: Recurrent or refractory pediatric solid tumors
investor_note: This completed academic Phase 2 trial evaluated the anti-angiogenic agent thalidomide combined with metronomic cyclophosphamide in heavily pre-treated pediatric solid tumors — a historically difficult-to-treat population. No primary outcome measures are recorded in the registry, limiting interpretability of results; the trial is of historical/scientific interest rather than near-term commercial relevance.

indication: Recurrent extremity soft tissue sarcoma (local recurrence)
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 surgical trial compares barrier resection (wide anatomic compartment excision) vs. standard 1 cm-margin wide local excision for local control in recurrent extremity soft tissue sarcoma — a population at elevated re-recurrence risk where no surgical standard exists. The primary completion date has long passed with status listed as UNKNOWN, raising serious concerns about trial completion and data availability; there is no commercial drug asset, limiting direct investor relevance.

indication: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), recurrent/metastatic, 1L
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored Phase 2 trial evaluates QL1706 (a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) combined with nab-paclitaxel ± bevacizumab as first-line therapy in r/mTNBC, with ORR as the primary signal-finding endpoint. The non-randomized, open-label design with only 60 patients limits interpretability — results would be hypothesis-generating for QL1706's developer (Qilu Pharma) rather than registrational evidence.

indication: Relapsed/refractory indolent B-cell lymphoma (follicular & marginal zone)
investor_note: This Phase 2 study evaluated whether adding bortezomib (a proteasome inhibitor) to rituximab (an anti-CD20 mAb) prolongs time-to-progression in relapsed/refractory indolent B-cell lymphoma — two mechanistically distinct agents making "combination" the appropriate modality call. The trial is now completed; with no formal comparator arm and a surrogate PFS endpoint, results are hypothesis-generating rather than registrational.

indication: Advanced solid tumors (locally advanced/unresectable or metastatic)
investor_note: This dose-escalation study of ASP1951 (alone and with pembrolizumab) in advanced solid tumors was designed to establish safety, PK, and RP2D/MTD — but was terminated before completion, materially undermining any path to Phase 2. The termination is the dominant investor signal: the program appears unlikely to advance, and no efficacy conclusions can be drawn from the available data.

indication: CML (CP, BP) and Ph+ ALL, ≥2L after prior TKI failure (Japanese patients)
investor_note: This Japan-specific Phase 1/2 study established the recommended dose and assessed efficacy (MCyR in CP-CML; MaHR in BP-CML/Ph+ ALL) of ponatinib in TKI-refractory patients, supporting a Japanese regulatory package for the drug. With only 35 enrolled patients across a non-randomized, open-label design, results are bridging/label-enabling in nature rather than independently registrational.

indication: Unspecified adult solid tumors (chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy prevention)
investor_note: This completed Phase 3 randomized, double-blind trial tested whether vitamin E supplementation reduces the incidence of ≥Grade 2 chemotherapy-induced sensory peripheral neuropathy versus placebo across unselected solid tumor patients on neurotoxic chemotherapy. As a dietary supplement intervention with no commercial sponsor, this trial carries minimal direct investment relevance but may inform supportive-care standard of practice and indirectly affect chemotherapy utilization patterns.

indication: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) in breast, GI, and gynecologic cancers
investor_note: This randomized, placebo-controlled trial aimed to assess whether twice-daily topical menthol reduces neuropathic pain (BPI-SF) in CIPN patients on taxane or platinum regimens, but was terminated after enrolling only 12 of its intended participants. The early termination and minimal accrual render the data inconclusive, making this trial of negligible investment relevance without a successor study.

indication: Glioblastoma multiforme (adult), 1L
investor_note: This completed NCI-sponsored pilot Phase 2 trial evaluated erlotinib (EGFR TKI) combined with standard temozolomide and radiotherapy in newly diagnosed GBM, with 52-week survival rate as the key near-term endpoint. As a single-arm, non-randomized study, any survival signal is hypothesis-generating only and cannot establish superiority over the Stupp standard of care without a randomized comparator.

indication: Unresectable renal cell carcinoma (RCC)
investor_note: This completed single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated the triplet combination of gemcitabine, capecitabine, and sorafenib in unresectable RCC, with PFS as the primary signal-finding endpoint. The small estimated enrollment of 40 patients, lack of a comparator arm, and academic sponsorship limit generalizability — results are hypothesis-generating only and would require randomized validation to be commercially actionable.

indication: Advanced NSCLC, 1L (elderly or ECOG PS 2 patients)
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 compared sequential erlotinib + gemcitabine vs. gemcitabine monotherapy as 1L therapy in frail/elderly advanced NSCLC patients, with PFS as the key endpoint. The trial was terminated early with only 54 of a planned 100–500 patients enrolled, rendering any efficacy conclusions unreliable and eliminating this as a meaningful catalyst.

indication: Locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
investor_note: This bioequivalence/PK study compares a generic gefitinib (CTTQ) to AstraZeneca's Iressa in NSCLC patients, with the goal of establishing comparable bioavailability to support regulatory approval of the biosimilar. The primary readout is PK parameters (AUC, Tmax, t½), not clinical efficacy — investor relevance is limited to generic market entry risk for AstraZeneca's Iressa franchise in China.

indication: Advanced cancer, refractory symptoms (pain, delirium, dyspnea, nausea) — palliative/terminal setting
investor_note: This pilot was designed solely to assess feasibility and recruitment rates for a future Phase 3 RCT comparing dexmedetomidine to midazolam for palliative symptom control — it was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient, meaning no data were generated. The trial is a dead catalyst; any investment thesis around dexmedetomidine in palliative oncology would require a new, independent study to be initiated.

indication: Advanced solid tumors (unselected), 1L/later lines
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD/safety profile of MPB-1734 across advanced solid tumors, with a Phase 2a expansion into sponsor-selected indications based on emerging data. The key catalyst is tolerability and any early efficacy signal from Part 2 cohorts, but the small per-cohort enrollment (≤15 patients) and single-arm, uncontrolled design limit the strength of any efficacy conclusions.

indication: HPV-associated (p16+) oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, post-operative
investor_note: This single-institution Phase 2 study tests whether ctDNA can guide de-escalation or intensification of post-operative cisplatin-based therapy in resected HPV+ oropharyngeal cancer, with 2-year PFS as the primary endpoint. Key caveats are the small, single-arm, non-randomized design at one site and a primary completion date nearly seven years out, making this a hypothesis-generating signal study rather than a registrational catalyst.

indication: Stage I-II lung cancer (surgical margin, brachytherapy-eligible)
investor_note: This feasibility study evaluates CivaSheet, a novel Pd-103 LDR brachytherapy implant, in early-stage lung cancer patients to demonstrate 1-year local control while sparing critical structures like the heart — a device-differentiation claim vs. standard brachytherapy seeds. With only 40 patients, no comparator arm, and a surrogate local control endpoint, results will be hypothesis-generating only and insufficient for broad regulatory or commercial conclusions without a larger controlled follow-on study.

indication: Stage IIIC node-positive endometrial cancer, 1L
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored Phase 1 trial evaluates the safety and tolerability of chemoradiation (cisplatin-based) followed by carboplatin/paclitaxel plus dostarlimab (PD-1 inhibitor) maintenance in locally advanced, node-positive endometrial cancer — the key catalyst is establishing a tolerable regimen that could underpin a larger efficacy study. With only 21 estimated enrollees and a safety-primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating, de-risking step rather than a registrational signal.

indication: Angiomyolipoma in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) and sporadic Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM)
investor_note: This completed long-term follow-up study assessed tolerability of everolimus (RAD001) in a small cohort of TSC/LAM patients with angiomyolipoma, with tumor growth inhibition/regression as a secondary hypothesis. With only 20 patients, a single arm, and tolerance as the primary endpoint, this is a signal-generating safety study — not a registrational trial — and its findings are most relevant as supportive evidence for the mTOR inhibitor class in rare TSC-related tumors.

indication: Inoperable/unresectable locally advanced NSCLC (LA-NSCLC)
investor_note: This single-arm academic study evaluated cetuximab (EGFR monoclonal antibody) combined with conformal thoracic radiotherapy followed by docetaxel/cetuximab consolidation in unresectable LA-NSCLC, with median PFS as the primary signal. With only 27 patients enrolled and no comparator arm, results are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no direct registrational weight.

indication: Poor-risk ALL or bilineage/biphenotypic leukemia, newly diagnosed/relapsed/refractory
investor_note: This completed NCI-sponsored Phase 1 dose-escalation trial established the MTD and toxicity profile of the HDAC inhibitor entinostat combined with clofarabine chemotherapy in poor-risk ALL; the primary catalyst was safety/MTD definition, not efficacy. With only 27 patients, a single arm, and a government sponsor, this is a hypothesis-generating study — any efficacy signals would require validation in a larger, controlled setting before commercial relevance.

indication: Locally advanced pancreatic cancer
investor_note: This randomized Phase 1/2 trial evaluates whether adding γδ T cell immunotherapy to irreversible electroporation (IRE) ablation improves PFS and OS in locally advanced pancreatic cancer — a setting with very limited treatment options. The trial is completed but was investigator-sponsored at a single Chinese center, limiting generalizability; results would be hypothesis-generating rather than registrational.

indication: Lung cancer (post-thoracoscopic surgery pain management)
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored dose-finding study evaluates two oxycodone doses combined with paravertebral nerve block for post-thoracoscopic analgesia in lung cancer patients, with the goal of identifying an optimal multimodal analgesic regimen; the primary endpoint (NRS pain scores at 24h) is a functional/symptom measure rather than an oncologic efficacy endpoint. This trial has limited direct investment relevance as it addresses perioperative pain management rather than antitumor activity, and the Phase 1 label likely reflects dose-optimization intent rather than traditional oncology dose-escalation.

indication: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), maintenance setting
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial tests whether thalidomide maintenance prolongs relapse-free survival in DLBCL versus observation, a clinically meaningful but non-OS endpoint in a setting with limited approved maintenance options. The trial's unknown status and estimated-only enrollment raise concerns about completion and data maturity, limiting near-term catalyst value.

indication: Advanced solid tumors (NSCLC, melanoma, SCCHN, TNBC, adrenocortical carcinoma, mesothelioma, high-MDSC), multiple lines
investor_note: This dose-escalation study evaluates eganelisib (IPI-549), a PI3K-gamma inhibitor targeting myeloid immunosuppression, as monotherapy and in combination with nivolumab across a broad range of advanced solid tumors; the key catalyst is establishing a safe RP2D and any early efficacy signal in biomarker-selected cohorts (e.g., high-MDSC). As a multi-part Phase 1 with non-randomized design and safety/tolerability primary endpoints, results are hypothesis-generating only and do not support registration without further controlled trials.

indication: Stage I/II prostate adenocarcinoma, neoadjuvant (pre-radical prostatectomy)
investor_note: This completed academic Phase 2 trial evaluated different soy isoflavone regimens as neoadjuvant chemoprevention in early prostate cancer, using oxidative DNA and lipid damage biomarkers — not clinical outcomes — as primary endpoints. With only 32 patients and surrogate biomarker endpoints, results are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no direct registrational or near-term commercial relevance.

indication: Cancer (high fall-risk, mixed tumor types)
investor_note: This exploratory, single-arm pilot tests a data-driven exercise prescription (pedometer + perturbation treadmill) to improve balance confidence in cancer patients at high fall risk, with the ABC Scale as the primary measure — not a clinical efficacy endpoint. The study is hypothesis-generating only; with 34 patients, no comparator, and a patient-reported balance scale as the primary outcome, it carries no near-term commercial catalyst value without a larger randomized follow-on.

indication: EGFR mutation+ advanced NSCLC, post-EGFR TKI (Chinese patients)
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 PK bridging study characterized the pharmacokinetics of AZD9291 (osimertinib) and its metabolites in Chinese EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients at 40 mg and 80 mg doses, supporting regulatory submissions in China. With only 31 patients and a PK/safety primary focus, this is a bridging/ethnic-sensitivity study rather than an efficacy catalyst — its value lies in enabling Chinese market approval for osimertinib.

indication: EGFR-mutant stage IB-IIIB non-squamous NSCLC, adjuvant (MRD-guided)
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored, MRD-guided study tests whether adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy directed by ctDNA/MRD status improves DFS in resected EGFR-mutant NSCLC, potentially validating MRD as a treatment-selection biomarker in the adjuvant setting. Key caveats are the non-randomized design and DFS surrogate endpoint, which limit regulatory applicability but could generate hypothesis-driving data for future registrational trials.

indication: Breast cancer risk reduction, premenopausal women (prevention/biomarker study)
investor_note: This completed single-arm study assessed whether the FDA-approved omega-3 formulation Lovaza™ can modulate blood and tissue biomarkers associated with breast cancer risk in premenopausal women, with the primary endpoint being treatment completion rate rather than a clinical efficacy outcome. As a small, non-randomized biomarker/feasibility study in healthy volunteers, results are hypothesis-generating only and carry no direct registrational or near-term commercial catalyst value.

indication: Metastatic breast cancer, biomarker-selected (genomically actionable alterations)
investor_note: This umbrella trial tests whether genome-guided matching of targeted agents (mTOR, FGFR, AKT, EGFR, MEK, RET inhibitors) improves PFS over standard maintenance chemo in metastatic breast cancer — a direct test of the precision-oncology hypothesis at scale. A positive PFS result would validate genomic triage as a treatment-selection strategy, though the open-label design and PFS-only primary limit regulatory weight; the academic sponsorship also means no single commercial asset is the primary beneficiary.

indication: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), occult invasive breast cancer detection
investor_note: This feasibility study evaluates whether [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/MRI can detect occult invasive cancer in DCIS patients prior to surgery, with histopathology as the reference standard. With only 30 patients and a single-arm academic design, results are hypothesis-generating only — the key watch item is diagnostic sensitivity/specificity data that could justify a larger, potentially registrational imaging trial.

indication: Chronic non-cancer pain (opioid-tolerant patients), primary care setting
investor_note: This pilot Phase 3 randomized trial tests whether ultra-low dose oral ketamine improves pain scores and function vs. placebo in opioid-tolerant chronic pain patients over just 2 weeks — a very short window that limits conclusions about durability. With only 32 estimated enrollees and an academic sponsor, this is hypothesis-generating at best; results would need replication in a larger, longer, industry-sponsored trial to be commercially actionable.

indication: Metastatic colorectal cancer, 1L
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation trial sought to establish the MTD and recommended Phase 2 dose of sorafenib combined with FOLFIRI as first-line therapy in mCRC; the primary catalyst was RP2D identification to enable a subsequent efficacy study. With only 16 patients enrolled and no comparator arm, findings are strictly hypothesis-generating and carry no direct registrational value.

indication: HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer with visceral metastasis, 1L
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial compares ribociclib + endocrine therapy vs. chemotherapy ± bevacizumab in HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer with visceral metastasis, with PFS as the primary endpoint — a head-to-head that could inform sequencing of CDK4/6 inhibitor-based regimens vs. chemo in this visceral-crisis subgroup. With only 41 patients actually enrolled, the study is severely underpowered for a definitive registrational conclusion, limiting any PFS findings to hypothesis-generating signal only.

indication: Relapsed prostate cancer
investor_note: This Phase 2 single-arm study of docetaxel in relapsed prostate cancer was terminated after enrolling only 3 patients, rendering it statistically uninformative and generating no actionable efficacy signal. The trial carries no residual investment relevance given its terminated status and near-zero accrual.

indication: Chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia, solid malignancy (pediatric/adolescent)
investor_note: This academic randomized controlled trial evaluates romiplostim (a thrombopoietin receptor agonist) for managing chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia in pediatric solid tumor patients, with hematologic response as the primary endpoint. With only 30 estimated enrollees and an academic sponsor, findings will be hypothesis-generating at best — not registrational — but could inform label-expansion interest for romiplostim in the pediatric oncology supportive care setting.

indication: Folate receptor-alpha+ ovarian cancer (intraoperative imaging)
investor_note: This first-in-human study tests whether EC17, a folate-receptor-targeted fluorescent probe, can reliably illuminate occult FR-alpha+ ovarian tumors intraoperatively — a proof-of-concept for a novel surgical imaging modality. With only 10 estimated enrollees and a detection-ability primary endpoint, this is purely a feasibility/signal-finding study; any positive result would need validation in larger, controlled trials before commercial relevance can be assessed.

indication: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), 1L
investor_note: This Phase 1/2 randomized trial evaluated cilengitide (an integrin inhibitor targeting tumor angiogenesis) added to standard temozolomide plus radiotherapy in newly diagnosed GBM, with Phase 1 establishing MTD/safety and Phase 2 comparing OS across dose arms. Now completed, the key investor read is whether cilengitide demonstrated an OS benefit over the standard-of-care backbone — a signal that would need replication in a larger registrational study to be commercially actionable.

indication: Ph+ chronic myelogenous leukemia, chronic phase (CML-CP), 1L
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial compares two doses of flumatinib (a next-gen BCR-ABL TKI) against imatinib in newly diagnosed Ph+ CML-CP, with major molecular response (MMR) at 6 months as the primary endpoint — a surrogate that could support dose selection and differentiation from imatinib. Primary completion has passed (H1 2012) with unknown status, so results may already exist but the trial's current disposition warrants verification before drawing investment conclusions.

indication: CD22+ relapsed/refractory leukemia and lymphoma
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored Phase 1 trial evaluates the safety and manufacturing feasibility of a CD22-targeted CAR T-cell therapy in heavily pre-treated, CD19-escape leukemia patients — a clinically meaningful niche with limited alternatives. With only 4 actual enrollees and a primary completion date already passed, this is a very early proof-of-concept signal; any commercial relevance hinges on whether safety and manufacturing success rates support advancement to a larger, sponsored efficacy study.

indication: Brain metastases (mixed primary tumors)
investor_note: This completed academic study evaluates whether DSC-perfusion MRI can predict local progression after Gamma Knife radiosurgery for brain metastases — a biomarker/imaging validation exercise rather than a therapeutic efficacy trial. With only 23 patients and no comparator, findings are hypothesis-generating only and carry no direct near-term commercial catalyst.

indication: Advanced angiosarcoma, post-immunotherapy progression
investor_note: This first-in-combination study pairs intratumoral oncolytic virus VO with pembrolizumab in a rare, IO-refractory sarcoma, with ORR as the key Phase 2 efficacy signal; a meaningful response rate in this heavily pretreated niche could support further development of VO in solid tumors. Key caveats are the very small single-arm enrollment (n=18), lack of a comparator, and a long timeline to primary readout in late 2029.

indication: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma/gliosarcoma, neoadjuvant, 1L
investor_note: WinGlio tests whether neoadjuvant CTLA-4 blockade (ipilimumab) is safe and feasible before standard surgery/chemoradiation in newly diagnosed GBM — a setting where checkpoint inhibitors have historically failed to show survival benefit. With only 16 patients and no comparator, this is a signal-generating feasibility study; the key watch item is tolerability and any radiographic response that could justify a larger randomized trial.

indication: EGFR-mutant advanced/metastatic NSCLC
investor_note: This trial of rociletinib (EGFR TKI) plus atezolizumab (MPDL3280A, PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor) in EGFR-mutant NSCLC was terminated after enrolling only 3 patients, rendering all findings non-interpretable. The termination, combined with rociletinib's well-documented clinical and regulatory failures at Clovis Oncology, makes this trial a cautionary case study with no residual investment catalyst.

indication: Resectable/potentially resectable Stage III NSCLC, neoadjuvant
investor_note: This randomized 3-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether adding a novel BTLA-targeting antibody (JS004) to a PD-1 inhibitor (toripalimab) plus platinum-based chemotherapy can meaningfully improve pCR rates over standard neoadjuvant IO-chemo in Stage III NSCLC — a positive result would validate the PD-1/BTLA dual checkpoint combination as a neoadjuvant strategy and support further registrational development. Key caveats are the academic/investigator-sponsored setting, pCR as a surrogate (not OS) primary endpoint, and the open-label design.

indication: NY-ESO-1+ advanced solid tumors and hematologic malignancies (multiple myeloma, melanoma, synovial sarcoma, myxoid/round cell liposarcoma)
investor_note: This first-in-human trial tested CRISPR-engineered, NY-ESO-1-redirected autologous T cells with endogenous TCR and PD-1 knockout — a landmark proof-of-concept for multiplex CRISPR editing in cell therapy — but was terminated with only 3 patients enrolled, severely limiting any efficacy or safety conclusions. The terminated status and minimal accrual mean this record is primarily of scientific/historical interest; investors should look to successor programs for clinical validation of this CRISPR cell therapy approach.

indication: Secondary brain malignancies (brain metastases), post-radiation — distinguishing tumor progression from radiation necrosis
investor_note: This pilot study evaluates whether 18F-fluciclovine PET/CT — already FDA-approved for recurrent prostate cancer — can accurately differentiate radiation necrosis from tumor progression in brain metastasis patients where MRI is inconclusive, with diagnostic accuracy (ROC AUC) as the primary endpoint. With only 18 patients enrolled and a completed status, results are hypothesis-generating at best; commercial relevance hinges on whether a label expansion into neuro-oncology imaging could be pursued by the agent's marketer.

indication: Medullary thyroid cancer
investor_note: This academic Phase 2 pilot evaluated lithium carbonate as a repurposed agent in medullary thyroid cancer, with tumor response rate (RECIST) as the primary endpoint — but the trial was terminated after enrolling only 5 patients, severely limiting any efficacy conclusions. The terminated status, minimal enrollment, and single-arm design make this a non-actionable catalyst with no investable signal.

indication: PIK3CA-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer, 3L+
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored Phase 1/2 trial tests whether alpelisib (PI3Kα inhibitor) combined with capecitabine can deliver meaningful PFS benefit in a biomarker-selected, heavily pre-treated mCRC population that has exhausted two prior standard chemotherapy lines. The single-arm, non-randomized design limits interpretability — any PFS signal would be hypothesis-generating only and would require a randomized confirmatory study to be commercially actionable.

indication: HER2-expressing advanced epithelial ovarian cancer, neoadjuvant
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 study tests RC48 (disitamab vedotin, a HER2-directed ADC) plus carboplatin as neoadjuvant therapy in HER2-expressing ovarian cancer, with complete resection rate as the primary endpoint — a positive result would provide early proof-of-concept for ADC-based neoadjuvant regimens in a biomarker-selected gynecologic oncology niche. Key caveats are the small, non-randomized design and an academic sponsor, making this signal-generating rather than registrational.

indication: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC), ≥3L (progression/recurrence after ≥2 prior lines)
investor_note: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial tests AL8326 tablets vs. placebo on OS in heavily pre-treated SCLC (≥3L), a high-unmet-need setting with few approved options; a positive OS result would support a registration filing for Advenchen. Key watch items are the long readout horizon (H2 2028), the relatively modest enrollment of 243 patients, and the limited public data on AL8326's mechanism and prior clinical evidence.

indication: Relapsed/refractory leukemia (AML, ALL, ATL, CML-BP, CLL, MDS, CMML)
investor_note: This dose-escalation study aimed to establish the MTD/DLT profile and PK of Terameprocol (EM-1421), a small molecule, in a broad leukemia population — but the trial was terminated early with only 16 patients enrolled, severely limiting any conclusions. The terminated status is a significant red flag, suggesting the program did not advance and the asset carries substantial development risk.

indication: metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC)
investor_note: This small investigator-sponsored Phase 1 trial evaluates whether bipolar androgen therapy (cycling testosterone between castrate and supraphysiological levels) can restore androgen receptor sensitivity in mCRPC, with AR activity as the primary biological endpoint rather than a clinical efficacy measure. With only 14 patients, no comparator, and a 2029 readout, this is a mechanistic/hypothesis-generating study — not a registrational catalyst.

indication: Melanoma (stage IIC–IV)
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation study evaluated safety and immune response of an autologous dendritic cell vaccine (DC/Apo-Nec) across four dose cohorts in 16 melanoma patients; the primary catalyst was tolerability confirmation and early immunogenicity signals, not efficacy. With only 16 patients, no comparator arm, and no primary completion date on record, this is strictly hypothesis-generating — any disease-free survival observations in stage III patients would require a randomized trial to validate.

indication: Resectable locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of head and neck (SCCHN), neoadjuvant/preoperative
investor_note: This window-of-opportunity study assesses whether a short preoperative course of atezolizumab (PD-L1 inhibitor) can modulate tumor-infiltrating immune cells in resectable SCCHN, with a secondary focus on feasibility and biomarker discovery — not efficacy. With only 20 patients and no comparator, findings are hypothesis-generating only, with translational value for identifying predictive biomarkers that could inform larger IO trials in this setting.

indication: AML / MDS in complete remission, elderly (≥65y), transplant-ineligible
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored Phase 2 (FLAT-Auto) tests whether a fludarabine/ARA-C/treosulfan conditioning regimen followed by autologous PBSCT can extend 2-year DFS in elderly AML/MDS patients unfit for allogeneic transplant — a feasibility and efficacy signal-finding study, not a registrational trial. With only 15 patients enrolled in a single-arm design, any positive DFS signal is hypothesis-generating at best and carries substantial risk of over-interpretation.

indication: Transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, 1L
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether intensified maintenance (lenalidomide + ixazomib + daratumumab) improves PFS over lenalidomide alone following a quadruplet induction in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed MM — a result that could support the commercial case for sustained daratumumab-based regimens in this population. With only 79 patients across two arms and PFS as the primary endpoint, the study is hypothesis-generating rather than registrational, and the small sample limits statistical power to detect a meaningful difference.

indication: ER+/HER2- early breast cancer (Stage I–III), endocrine therapy-related musculoskeletal pain
investor_note: This EORTC-led pragmatic Phase 3 trial tests whether duloxetine or furosemide can meaningfully reduce endocrine therapy-related musculoskeletal pain — a key driver of treatment discontinuation — in ER+/HER2- early breast cancer, with QoL (EORTC QLQ-BR42 skeletal scale) as the primary endpoint. A positive result could support label expansion or guideline adoption for these repurposed agents, though the open-label design, QoL-based primary endpoint, and academic sponsorship limit near-term commercial catalyst value.

indication: MSS advanced/metastatic colorectal cancer
investor_note: This completed Phase 2 trial tested whether adding vicriviroc (a CCR5 antagonist) to pembrolizumab could unlock IO activity in MSS CRC — a historically immunotherapy-resistant population — across two dose levels. With only 41 actual enrollees and ORR as the primary efficacy endpoint, any signal would be hypothesis-generating only; the key watch is whether the combination achieved meaningful response rates in this difficult-to-treat, biomarker-defined subset.

indication: Metastatic or locally advanced cancer (mixed solid tumors)
investor_note: This completed cardiac safety study assessed whether ridaforolimus (an mTOR inhibitor) prolongs the QTc interval at supratherapeutic (100 mg) and therapeutic (40 mg) doses in advanced cancer patients — a regulatory requirement, not an efficacy signal. The result is a binary de-risking event: a clean QTc profile supports continued development, while a meaningful QTc prolongation would have been a significant safety liability for the program.

indication: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma, post-ICI therapy
investor_note: This trial was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient (actual enrollment = 0), meaning no efficacy or safety data for the PAC-1 + nivolumab combination in ICI-refractory mRCC will be generated from this study. The withdrawn status renders this record a non-event from an investment catalyst standpoint; any future development of this combination would require a new trial initiation.

indication: Advanced/metastatic pediatric solid tumors (multiple histologies)
investor_note: This completed Eli Lilly pediatric dose-finding study evaluated olaratumab (a PDGFRα-targeting mAb) alone and in combination with standard chemotherapy backbones to establish a recommended pediatric dose and safety profile. The catalyst was identification of a tolerable RP2D to enable future pediatric efficacy studies; however, olaratumab's subsequent Phase 3 failure in adult soft-tissue sarcoma (ANNOUNCE) substantially limits the commercial relevance of any pediatric signal generated here.

indication: HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (PI3K-activated and unselected), 2L+
investor_note: This randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 trial evaluated whether adding BKM120 (buparlisib), a pan-PI3K inhibitor, to weekly paclitaxel improves PFS in HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with a pre-specified PI3K-activated subgroup as a key analysis. The trial is completed, so results are available; the pivotal question for investors is whether PI3K pathway selection enriched for benefit, as pan-PI3K inhibitors have historically faced tolerability and efficacy hurdles in this setting.

indication: High-risk postmenopausal women, breast cancer chemoprevention
investor_note: This completed, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial evaluated anastrozole (an aromatase inhibitor) as a chemoprevention agent in postmenopausal women at elevated breast cancer risk, with incidence of invasive and non-invasive breast cancer as the primary endpoint. Results from this landmark IBIS-II trial are already mature; the key investor read-through is the established efficacy signal supporting aromatase inhibitor use in the prevention setting, though the indication targets healthy volunteers rather than a treatment population, limiting direct commercial applicability.

indication: Progressive or relapsing PVNS/TGCT (inoperable)
investor_note: This completed single-arm Phase 2 trial assessed nilotinib (a BCR-ABL/CSF1R TKI) in inoperable PVNS/TGCT, a rare benign-but-destructive joint tumor driven by CSF1R signaling; the non-progression rate at 12 weeks is the key efficacy signal. As a small, non-randomized, open-label academic study in a rare indication, results are hypothesis-generating rather than registrational, and the trial has already completed — any investor interest centers on published outcome data rather than a future catalyst.

indication: Nonmetastatic breast cancer, neoadjuvant
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial tests whether adding bevacizumab to a standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy backbone (FEC/docetaxel) improves pCR in nonmetastatic breast cancer — a surrogate endpoint with historically mixed translation to OS benefit for bevacizumab in this setting. The trial's UNKNOWN status and estimated-only enrollment of 800 raise questions about completion and data maturity; primary readout was estimated for H1 2012, suggesting results, if available, are long overdue or the trial may not have fully reported.

indication: Colorectal cancer lung metastases
investor_note: This feasibility study evaluates whether SGM-101, a CEA-targeted fluorescent tracer, can intraoperatively detect colorectal lung metastases using near-infrared imaging — a surgical guidance application rather than a therapeutic one. With only 10 patients and a non-efficacy primary endpoint, this is a proof-of-concept signal only; commercial relevance hinges on whether Surgimab can parlay feasibility data into a broader surgical oncology indication.

indication: Advanced solid tumors (breast, head & neck, NSCLC, prostate, gastric/GEJ)
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD and RP2D of OCT-598 as monotherapy and in combination with docetaxel across multiple solid tumor types; the key catalyst is safety/tolerability data and identification of a viable RP2D to advance into Phase 2. With only ~51 patients across 9 arms and no efficacy primary endpoint, this is a pure de-risking step — any early anti-tumor signal would be hypothesis-generating only.

indication: Advanced biliary tract cancer, 1L
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored, single-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether adding the PD-1 inhibitor toripalimab to an S-1 plus nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy backbone can generate a meaningful ORR in first-line advanced biliary tract cancer — a setting with limited approved options. With only ~30 estimated patients, no comparator arm, and an already-passed primary completion date with unknown status, results are hypothesis-generating at best and carry significant reliability and generalizability risk.

indication: Progressive metastatic androgen-independent (castration-resistant) prostate adenocarcinoma
investor_note: This Phase 2 investigator-sponsored trial evaluates lutetium Lu 177-labeled anti-PSMA monoclonal antibody J591 in castration-resistant metastatic prostate cancer, with PSA response at 8 weeks as the primary endpoint — a biochemical surrogate that would support further development of radioimmunotherapy in this setting. Key caveats are the single-arm design, surrogate PSA endpoint (not OS or PFS), and missing enrollment and completion date data, limiting the ability to size the signal or project a readout timeline.

indication: Operable locally-regionally advanced melanoma, neoadjuvant
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether intratumoral tavokinogene telseplasmid delivered via electroporation (Tavo-EP) combined with nivolumab can achieve pathologic complete response in resectable advanced melanoma, a neoadjuvant setting where pCR correlates with long-term outcomes. With only 17 patients enrolled and no comparator arm, results are hypothesis-generating only — a strong pCR rate would support further development of the Tavo-EP/IO combination but cannot establish superiority over standard neoadjuvant IO approaches.

indication: MSLN-positive advanced solid tumors (NSCLC, mesothelioma)
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored early-phase dose-escalation study evaluates the safety and tolerability of a novel armored CAR-T construct (anti-MSLN CAR T cells engineered to secrete PD-1 nanobodies) in a small cohort of 10 patients — the sole catalyst is DLT/tolerability data and any early signals of anti-tumor activity. With only 10 estimated enrollees, a single academic site, and an unknown current status, this is a pure hypothesis-generating safety study with no near-term registrational relevance.

indication: Advanced solid tumors (sarcoma, melanoma, HNSCC, breast, cervical, vulvar, penile, anal cancers)
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation study evaluates the safety, tolerability, and PK profile of Stimotimagene copolymerplasmid — a gene therapy plasmid encoding HSV-TK paired with ganciclovir — across a broad basket of solid tumors; the key catalyst is establishing a clean safety/DLT profile and RP2D to enable focused Phase 2 development. With only 21 patients enrolled across a heterogeneous tumor basket and no efficacy primary endpoint, this is purely a safety/PK de-risking step with no near-term registrational read-through.

indication: Advanced unresectable pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNET)
investor_note: This Phase 1/2 academic study sought to establish the MTD/RP2D of temozolomide plus pazopanib and then assess ORR in advanced unresectable PNET; a meaningful ORR at the RP2D would provide hypothesis-generating support for the combination in this niche indication. With only 29 patients enrolled, a non-randomized single-arm design, and no active comparator, results are signal-finding only and not registrational.

indication: Relapsed or refractory pediatric solid tumors or lymphoma
investor_note: This completed NCI-sponsored pediatric Phase 1 trial established the MTD and safety profile of ispinesib (a kinesin spindle protein inhibitor) in heavily pre-treated children with relapsed/refractory solid tumors or lymphoma. As a government-run, dose-finding study with 30 patients and no efficacy primary endpoint, it is a foundational safety data point only — not a commercial catalyst.

indication: Follicular lymphoma (FL), 1L previously untreated
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluates the BTK inhibitor zanubrutinib added to the obinutuzumab-CVP backbone in untreated FL, with MRD-guided maintenance as a secondary exploratory angle; a high complete response rate (CRR) would support further development of BTK inhibition in 1L FL. Key caveats are the small 40-patient enrollment, lack of a comparator arm, and use of CRR (a surrogate) as the primary endpoint — results would be hypothesis-generating only, not registrational.

indication: Advanced solid tumors (unselected)
investor_note: This completed first-in-human study evaluated the safety and tolerability of FP-1039, a biologic (FGFR1-Fc fusion protein) across advanced cancers with no biomarker selection or efficacy primary endpoint. As a Phase 1 dose-escalation study with only 39 patients, the value is limited to safety de-risking and any early signals of activity that could inform subsequent biomarker-selected development.

indication: locally advanced or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma (L-sarcoma), 2L+
investor_note: This two-part China-specific study sought to establish the optimal trabectedin dose in Chinese L-sarcoma patients (Part 1) and then confirm OS superiority over dacarbazine (Part 2); however, actual enrollment of only 16 patients suggests Part 2 was likely underpowered or not fully executed, severely limiting any OS conclusion. Investors should treat this as a regional dose-finding/bridging exercise rather than a standalone registrational dataset.

indication: ALK or ROS1 fusion+ newly-diagnosed high-grade glioma (pediatric), 1L
investor_note: This pediatric early-phase study tests lorlatinib — a CNS-penetrant ALK/ROS1 TKI — in a rare, biomarker-selected, and historically lethal pediatric brain tumor population, with disease control rate and safety as co-primary endpoints across four treatment arms. The extremely small enrollment (n=15), non-randomized design, and surrogate endpoint limit registrational relevance, but a strong disease control signal in this fusion-driven niche could justify accelerated development and attract partnership interest.

indication: Advanced RCC, GIST, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
investor_note: This dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD, DLTs, and RP2D of hypoxia-activated prodrug TH-302 combined with sunitinib across three tumor types, with a dose-expansion cohort providing preliminary efficacy signal in advanced RCC. As a completed early-phase, single-arm study with an unknown current status, the primary investor value lies in whether the RP2D and tolerability data were sufficient to support a Phase 2 program — not in registrational-level efficacy evidence.

indication: Head and neck cancer, radiation-induced oral mucositis prevention
investor_note: This NCI-sponsored Phase 3 randomized trial aimed to determine whether iseganan HCl oral solution could prevent oral mucositis in head and neck cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy, a meaningful supportive-care endpoint. The record is severely incomplete — no primary outcomes, enrollment figures, masking, or primary completion date are documented, and the unknown status raises serious concerns about whether the trial was ever completed or terminated.

indication: Unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), 1L
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether adding a PD-L1 inhibitor (adebrelimab) and low-dose bevacizumab to locoregional TACE-HAIC can generate a compelling first-line ORR in unresectable HCC, using Simon's two-stage design to gate further development. Key caveats are the small 38-patient enrollment, absence of a comparator arm, and a primary readout not expected until H2 2029 — making this a signal-generating, not registrational, study.

indication: Oncology (healthy volunteer, formulation/PK study)
investor_note: This completed first-in-human SAD/MAD and formulation bioavailability study in healthy male volunteers establishes the safety, tolerability, and PK profile of EXS21546 — a prerequisite step before oncology patient dosing. The trial is purely a pharmacological/formulation de-risking exercise with no efficacy signal; investor relevance is limited to confirmation of a viable oral solid-dose formulation advancing into cancer patients.

indication: Metastatic breast cancer, 1L
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial sought to determine whether adding capecitabine to a taxane/bevacizumab backbone improved PFS in first-line metastatic breast cancer, but the trial was terminated before completion, rendering its primary endpoint uninterpretable. The terminated status and estimated (not actual) enrollment of 432 make any efficacy conclusions unreliable; this trial is not a viable catalyst.

indication: Relapsed/refractory locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, including TNBC
investor_note: This dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD of oral OTS167 (a MELK kinase inhibitor) in heavily pre-treated breast cancer patients, including the hard-to-treat TNBC subset; the key catalyst is identification of a tolerable RP2D that enables a subsequent efficacy study. Pure Phase 1 risk with a long projected timeline to primary completion — meaningful only as a safety/dose-finding milestone, not an efficacy readout.

indication: DLL3+ glioblastoma / DIPG / diffuse midline glioma
investor_note: This first-in-indication Phase 1/2 study will establish the safety profile and early efficacy signal of a DLL3-targeted CAR-T (4SCAR DLL3) in a biomarker-selected, high-unmet-need pediatric/adult brain tumor population including GBM and DIPG/DMG. With only 30 patients, no comparator, and a safety-primary design, any efficacy readout will be hypothesis-generating only — the key watch is tolerability and CAR-T persistence in the CNS compartment.

indication: Gastric cancer, postoperative (age ≥55)
investor_note: This randomized, quadruple-masked Phase 3 trial evaluates whether perioperative dexmedetomidine improves postoperative sleep duration, pain relief, and recovery in middle-aged and elderly gastric cancer patients. The primary endpoint (sleep time) is non-standard and non-registrational, limiting commercial relevance; the trial is best viewed as a supportive quality-of-recovery study for an already-generic sedative agent.
